children: The S&P Global Flash Australia Manufacturing PMI was confirmed at 52.0 in August 2026, unchanged from the preliminary estimate, matching July's reading and remaining at the highest level since January.
A reading above 50 indicates growth, signalling a further modest improvement in the overall health of the sector.
The latest figure was supported by a faster rise in new orders since January, amid renewed export growth.
Employment increased for the fourth month running.
As a result, firms reduced their backlogs of work, which fell markedly and by the largest extent in just over a year.
However, output ticked lower, reversing a slight rise seen in July, as demand remained muted.
On the price front, input cost inflation accelerated slightly due to higher freight and fuel costs, while output cost inflation eased for the third straight month and was the slowest in seven months.
Suppliers' delivery times lengthened due to international shipping delays.

title: Australia Manufacturing Growth Confirmed at 6-Month High
